newsitem.title: USA: Sparks head warns U.S. grain of self-reliant Asia.
newsitem.headline: Sparks head warns U.S. grain of self-reliant Asia.

text.p: Too much self-sufficiency in Asia could be devastating for the U.S. grain industry, the head of agricultural analytical firm Sparks Companies Inc warned American agribusiness leaders.

Carroll Brunthaver, president and chief executive officer of Sparks, based in Memphis, told members of the National Grain and Feed Association's committee on international trade that U.S. policy makers should avoid encouraging more self-reliance in Asia, especially China.
"Asia is so important to this industry...We have to be careful we don't do anything to force them to be more self- reliant and turn their backs on trade," Brunthaver said.
Brunthaver said that not renewing MFN for China would be a big mistake and said negotiators had to be careful in the ongoing talks with China over its entry into the World Trade Organization.
He said officials needed to make sure they were not jeopardizing long term demand for U.S. products by insisting that China make short term market access changes.

He added that reports by well-known agricultural economist Lester Brown that China's food demands will grow dramatically over the next few years and could drain the world of surplus grain stocks have actually been a disservice to the United States by pointing out to China that it needs to increase its agricultural production.
